english.notes:
From 20th October 2014, the power to make a closure order under section 11B of the Anti-social Behaviour Act 2003 is no longer in force. The repeal does not, however, apply in relation to an order made before that date or anything done in connection with such an order. As such, this offence can still be committed in relation to an order made before 20th October 2014.

Sections 11D(4) of the Anti-social Behaviour Act 2003 provides that a person who has a reasonable excuse for entering or being on the premises does not commit an offence.

other.penalty:
Summary: 51 Weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.Note:
In relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003, the reference in subsection (3)(a) to 51 weeks is to be read as a reference to 6 months

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
